do_not_assume: Category security protects the request.
Expiration is a deletion policy.
Automatic approval is safe merely because flagging is enabled.
Public submissions enter the intended category and do not reach the prayer team without the chosen approval gate.
goal: Public submissions enter the intended category and do not reach the prayer team without the chosen approval gate.
steps: Open the external Prayer Request Entry block.
Set the category parent and default category deliberately.
Choose whether category selection is visible.
Decide whether automatic approval is appropriate.
If automatic approval is enabled, set the supported expiration period and establish a flagged-request review cadence.
Configure urgent, comments, and public-display choices.
Review which prayer attributes are public.
Submit test requests covering ordinary, urgent, private, comment-disabled, and sensitive cases.
Verify administrative state and prayer-team visibility for each test.
title: Recipe: Configure moderated public prayer intake

do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: Flagged and unapproved requests receive documented human disposition.
steps: Filter the prayer-request list for unapproved requests.
Filter or sort for flagged requests.
Open each request and review its text, public status, urgency, category, expiration, and flags.
Edit sensitive or inaccurate text only under the organization’s ministry policy.
Choose a disposition: remain unapproved, re-approve, or delete.
If re-approving, confirm that flags clear and the request re-enters the intended team scope.
Review the Prayer Comments list separately for comment moderation.
title: Recipe: Operate the administrator moderation queue

do_not_assume: Category security flows to request records.
Page access automatically grants comment-entry rights.
A small maximum-results value still gives the team complete coverage.
goal: A ministry team sees only the intended category scope through a secured page.
steps: Create or select a page for the ministry prayer team.
Restrict page access to the intended security role.
Add Prayer Session or Prayer Card View.
Configure the block for the ministry’s category.
Decide whether the block should show public requests only.
Configure flagging, threshold, ordering, and maximum results.
Test with an administrator, intended team member, unrelated signed-in person, and anonymous visitor.
Confirm that the administrative Prayer Request List remains restricted to administrators.
title: Recipe: Build a secured ministry-specific prayer queue

do_not_assume: The entry page will visibly identify the group.
An incorrect group association can be edited later.
Possession of the GUID alone is an adequate authorization design.
The request is associated with the wrong group; do not continue creating production requests through that URL.
goal: New requests are permanently associated with the correct group and appear only through that group’s prayer route.
steps: Resolve the intended group’s GUID through an authorized administrative method.
Construct the Prayer Request Entry URL with `GroupGuid`.
Verify the target group before distributing the URL.
Submit a non-sensitive test request.
Confirm the group association in administrative request details.
Open the Prayer Session or Prayer Card View route with the same parameter.
Confirm the test request appears.
Remove the parameter and confirm the group request is excluded.
Test surrounding page security with member, nonmember, and anonymous accounts.
Confirm the request was created with the intended `GroupGuid`.
Inspect the request’s group from its administrative details.
Remember that the association cannot be changed or removed after creation.
Confirm the prayer page URL carries the same `GroupGuid`.
Confirm the page uses Prayer Session or Prayer Card View.
Test as an intended group member.
Test as a signed-in nonmember and anonymous visitor to validate the surrounding access controls.
title: Recipe: Create and verify a group prayer route

do_not_assume: The person profile’s current email is the destination.
Comment permission and digest eligibility are the same control.
An unsaved communication was not sent.
goal: Allowed comments are delivered to request-specific email addresses within the intended category scope.
steps: Configure a scheduled job using the Send Prayer Comments job type.
Select the Prayer Request Comments Digest system communication.
For all categories, leave Prayer Categories blank and enable Include Child Categories.
For a narrower scope, select categories and explicitly choose child inclusion.
Decide whether sent communications should be saved.
Confirm test requests have Allow Comments enabled.
Add a non-sensitive test comment.
Run the job in a controlled test.
Verify the digest includes the original request and expected comments.
Verify delivery to the email stored on the request.
Run the job again after adding another comment and confirm it sends only comments added since the prior run.
Confirm the Send Prayer Comments job exists, is configured, and has run successfully.
Confirm the request has Allow Comments enabled.
Inspect the job’s category selection and Include Child Categories setting.
Inspect the email stored on the prayer request rather than relying on the person’s current profile email.
Confirm that a new comment exists within the job’s unsent window.
Inspect the configured system communication and outbound communication provider.
Determine whether Save Communications is enabled before expecting a saved communication record.
Perform a bounded test with non-sensitive content and verify receipt.
title: Recipe: Enable prayer-comment digests

do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: A qualifying prayer event creates a bounded care action without exposing the request broadly.
steps: Choose the supported trigger: request submission, Prayer Card prayed action, or Prayer Card flagged action.
Define the workflow’s entity and required attributes.
For Prayer Card actions, define the appropriate actor attribute: `PrayerOfferedByPersonId` or `FlaggedByPersonId`.
Add explicit criteria for the ministry condition being handled.
Assign the resulting activity only to authorized care workers.
Limit communication content to the minimum necessary.
Add an auditable completion or disposition state.
Test with synthetic requests that should and should not trigger.
Verify that unauthorized users cannot open the workflow or linked request.
title: Recipe: Add workflow-based care follow-up

do_not_assume: AI inheritance reaches grandchildren.
A non-public result is also unapproved.
AI moderation satisfies crisis or safeguarding procedures.
goal: AI processing is limited to known categories and produces reviewable results.
steps: Confirm an active AI provider.
Select a small pilot category.
Configure only the required capabilities.
If using inheritance, keep the pilot to direct child categories or configure deeper categories individually.
Confirm the entry block’s default category supports the intended automatic-categorization scope.
Enable an AI disclaimer where appropriate.
Submit synthetic examples covering names, formatting, private content, public appropriateness, and moderation concerns.
Compare processed text with the original.
Inspect public status, flag count, category, sentiment, and moderation results.
Establish a human review owner before broadening the scope.
title: Recipe: Introduce AI assistance with human review

do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: A signed-in mobile user can see, complete, and receive reminders for an assigned prayer touchpoint.
steps: Confirm the target server and mobile versions.
Confirm the Outreach Toolbox page is placed in the mobile shell.
Verify authentication and permissions for a pilot user.
Complete onboarding with known assignment days and reminder preferences.
Configure a test contact and prayer cadence.
Verify the dashboard shows the due action.
Complete the touchpoint and inspect its history.
Configure and run the applicable reminder job.
Verify the push notification on the target device.
Review who can see contact details, history, and pulse updates.
Confirm the request saved successfully.
Inspect whether it is approved. If automatic approval is disabled, approve it through the administrative request list.
Confirm it is active and inspect its expiration date.
Check whether the team block is scoped to a different category.
Check whether Public Only is enabled while the request is non-public.
Inspect its flag count and whether the configured threshold unapproved it.
Determine whether it is group-associated. A normal session without `GroupGuid` excludes group requests.
Inspect the block’s maximum-results and ordering settings.
Test the page using the affected team member’s exact permissions.
title: Recipe: Validate Outreach Toolbox for prayer touchpoints
